NDT training in Atlanta: how it works for Atlanta employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Atlanta technicians and employers at Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. The classroom portion is delivered live online, and hands-on practical training is delivered onsite at your facility anywhere in metro Atlanta or Georgia, under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you under its written practice after training, experience, exams and a vision test. Quotes on request.

Atlanta is not a refinery town, and that is exactly why NDT training here needs its own plan. The metro's inspection work is dominated by aviation maintenance at and around Hartsfield-Jackson, aerospace manufacturing in Cobb County, power generation across Georgia, one of the busiest fuel pipeline systems in the country, a heavy construction pipeline of data centres, warehouses and transport projects, and the fabrication shops that serve all of them. A technician in Atlanta is more likely to be inspecting a turbine component, an airframe, a structural weld on a new data centre, or a heat-exchanger bundle than a crude unit.

Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Atlanta. We deliver theory live online and bring practical sessions to your shop, hangar or plant. This section explains the courses, the certification path, the local regulators and what Atlanta employers look for. Request an Atlanta training quote and we will reply with cohort and onsite options within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Atlanta

Each course follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A and is offered at Level I, Level II, and as Level III examination preparation. The table shows how Atlanta-area employers typically use each method. It is market context, not a hiring guarantee.

MethodLevelsWhat Atlanta employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (Ultrasonic Testing)I, II, III prepAircraft structure and component inspection, structural weld inspection on commercial construction, power-plant piping and pressure-vessel thickness surveysLevel I: employer entry rules; Level II: Level I plus experience per written practice
PAUT (Phased Array UT)II, III prepWeld inspection on power-plant and industrial piping, corrosion mapping, composite and aerospace applicationsUT Level II (or concurrent) recommended
TOFD (Time of Flight Diffraction)II, III prepHeavy-wall weld sizing on vessels and power-generation componentsUT Level II recommended
RT (Radiographic Testing)I, II, III prepPipeline and piping weld radiography, casting inspection, fabrication-shop RTGeorgia radiation safety requirements apply separately
MT (Magnetic Particle Testing)I, II, III prepStructural steel on data-centre and warehouse builds, landing gear and ferritic aircraft parts, fabrication weldsEmployer entry rules
PT (Liquid Penetrant Testing)I, II, III prepEngine and airframe components, stainless piping, machined and cast partsEmployer entry rules
VT (Visual Testing)I, II, III prepStructural welding inspection, bridge and transport structures, plant condition surveys, aircraft visual checksEmployer entry rules
ET (Eddy Current Testing)I, II, III prepAircraft skins, fastener holes, wheels and engine components; condenser and heat-exchanger tubing in power plantsEmployer entry rules

UT course content. Ultrasonic physics, transducers and wedges, calibration, thickness measurement, angle-beam weld inspection, DAC and TCG, flaw characterisation and reporting. For Atlanta technicians we give extra attention to thin-section and bonded-structure inspection, because so much local work is aviation and light fabrication rather than heavy process piping.

PAUT and TOFD content. Phased-array beam forming, focal laws, sectorial and linear scans, encoded data collection, scan plans, TOFD geometry and interpretation. These methods matter most for power-generation and industrial piping work around the state.

ET content. Impedance-plane interpretation, probe selection, surface and bolt-hole inspection, conductivity and coating measurement, and tubing inspection concepts. ET is one of the most in-demand methods in Atlanta because of the size of the local aviation maintenance sector.

RT, MT, PT and VT content. Method theory, equipment, technique, acceptance criteria and reporting. Level III candidates receive structured preparation for the Basic, Method and Specific examinations; see ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Atlanta, step by step

Georgia does not issue an NDT licence. Under SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies. The steps are:

  1. Employer written practice. It sets the training, experience, exams and pass marks for each method and level.
  2. Formal classroom training in the method, delivered by Atlantis NDT live online or onsite. See recommended minimums in the training-requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience, documented and supervised by certified personnel.
  4. General examination covering method principles.
  5. Specific examination covering your employer's equipment, procedures and acceptance criteria.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens, administered under a Level III.
  7. Vision examination, near-vision and colour contrast, typically every year.
  8. Employer certification with Level III approval.
  9. Recertification at the interval set in the written practice.

More detail is in our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Atlanta crews

  • Live online classroom. Instructor-led in real time, so technicians working shifts at a hangar or a plant can train without losing a week to travel or Atlanta traffic. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility. Practical training at your shop, hangar or plant anywhere in Georgia, with your equipment and procedures and under Level III oversight. Ask about onsite training for your Atlanta crew.
  • Dedicated cohorts when several people are ready together.

Scheduling around local peaks. Aviation maintenance runs around heavy-check schedules; Georgia power plants schedule spring and fall outages; construction projects have fixed inspection hold points. We schedule theory in quieter weeks and practicals outside your peak windows. Share your calendar and we will build around it.

The practical exam is always on real specimens under a Level III, never online.

Where NDT technicians work in Atlanta

  • Aviation maintenance. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International is the hub for Delta Air Lines, whose TechOps maintenance organisation is one of the largest in North America, and the airport supports many other maintenance, component-repair and parts businesses. Airline and repair-station NDT relies heavily on ET, UT, PT, MT and VT. Aviation employers commonly work to NAS 410 or similar aerospace personnel standards; Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only, but the method skills are the same foundation.
  • Aerospace manufacturing. Lockheed Martin's Marietta site in Cobb County builds C-130J aircraft, and Georgia has a broad aerospace supply chain. Further south, Robins Air Force Base at Warner Robins is a major Air Force depot maintenance centre.
  • Power generation. Georgia's generating fleet includes Plant Vogtle near Waynesboro, where Units 3 and 4 were the first new US nuclear units built in decades, Plant Hatch, and large fossil plants such as Plant Bowen and Plant Scherer. Outages bring demand for UT, ET on condenser and heat-exchanger tubing, MT and PT. Nuclear work carries additional plant-specific qualification requirements.
  • Pipelines. Colonial Pipeline, one of the largest refined-products pipeline systems in the US, is headquartered in Alpharetta, and interstate gas and products lines cross Georgia. Pipeline construction and repair welding is commonly inspected to API 1104.
  • Construction and structural steel. Metro Atlanta has been one of the most active data-centre and distribution-warehouse markets in the US. Structural steel inspection on those builds typically references AWS D1.1, and the Georgia DOT bridge programme uses AWS D1.5, calling for VT, MT and UT.
  • Manufacturing and fabrication. Tank, vessel and skid fabricators work to ASME Section VIII and B31.3 with ASME Section V techniques. The state's growing automotive, battery and solar manufacturing base, and the Port of Savannah industrial corridor, add further demand for travelling technicians.

Radiography licensing in Georgia. Georgia is an NRC Agreement State, so radioactive materials used for industrial radiography are licensed by the state rather than the NRC, through the Radioactive Materials Program of the Georgia Environmental Protection Division; X-ray equipment is also subject to state registration. Companies need the appropriate licence or registration, and radiographers need the radiographer certification and radiation safety training the rules require. Our RT course is about technique and interpretation, not that regulatory qualification. Confirm current requirements with the state programme and your company's radiation safety officer.

What Atlanta employers typically ask for. Aviation roles ask for Level II in ET, UT and PT with aerospace-standard qualification on top. Construction inspection firms ask for UT, MT and VT, often alongside AWS CWI. Plant and pipeline contractors list UT, PAUT and RT, and some inspector roles ask for API credentials. Atlantis does not offer CWI, API or NAS 410 programmes. For pay context, see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Atlanta NDT companies

Small construction-inspection firms, fabrication shops and in-house QC teams around Atlanta often need Level III support without a full-time hire. We offer:

  • Written practice development tailored to your methods and clients. See NDT written practice development.
  • Procedures for UT, PAUT, TOFD, MT, PT, VT, ET and RT technique, aligned to the ASME, API or AWS documents your clients reference.
  • Level III examinations and audit-ready certification files.
  • Corporate training programmes for whole teams. See corporate NDT training.

Book a Level III consultation, or start with our SNT-TC-1A guidance.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets you practise 12 NDT methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Atlanta aviation technicians will get the most from the hangar scenes; construction and fabrication inspectors from the welding workshop.

It is practice only. It does not replace hands-on training with real equipment or the practical examination on real specimens under a Level III.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who designs the curriculum and oversees onsite programmes and exam content.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Atlanta

How do I get NDT certified in Atlanta?

Join or be sponsored by an employer that certifies under SNT-TC-1A, complete the training and experience its written practice requires, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III and a vision test, and the employer certifies you. We provide the training and exam preparation.

Can I take NDT training online in Georgia?

Yes, the classroom portion is delivered live online. The practical training and practical exam need real equipment and specimens, so they happen onsite at your employer or an arranged location. See online NDT training.

Is there an NDT training centre in Atlanta?

Atlantis NDT does not operate a physical centre in Atlanta. We deliver online and onsite at employers' facilities across Georgia.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

That depends on your employer's written practice, your starting level and your work schedule. See the SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums in our training-requirements matrix; we then fit the classroom hours to your shifts.

Do I need a license for radiography in Georgia?

Georgia is an Agreement State, so industrial radiography with radioactive materials is licensed by the state, and X-ray equipment is registered with the state. Radiographers need the certification and radiation safety training the rules require. Ask the state programme and your radiation safety officer for current requirements.

What does NDT training cost in Atlanta?

We do not publish prices. The quote depends on method, level, group size and online or onsite delivery. Request a quote; we reply within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Atlanta employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most common personnel qualification basis among US industrial and construction employers, and aviation employers build their aerospace qualification on the same method knowledge. Certification is issued by the employer.

Which NDT method is best for aviation jobs in Atlanta?

ET is the most aviation-specific method, with UT and PT close behind. Aviation employers usually add their own aerospace qualification requirements on top.

Can you train our team before a power-plant outage?

Yes. Theory goes online ahead of the outage and practical sessions are scheduled outside it. Nuclear sites define additional requirements through their own programmes.

Do you offer CWI or NAS 410 training in Atlanta?

No. Atlantis NDT trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Other credentials are issued by the relevant bodies or employers.

How can I practise for the practical exam?

Rehearse with the Practical NDT simulator, then build hands-on hours with real equipment. The exam is on real specimens under a Level III.

Where can I find UT Level 2 practice questions?

See our UT Level 2 practice questions and the mock exams in each course.
